dedupe_keys.name: rain pan european gridded data sets of extreme weather probability of occurrence under present and future climate

description: The RAIN project publishes European hazard probability outputs for infrastructure-network risk analysis. Native members cover coastal and river flooding, precipitation, freezing rain, snow, windstorms, tornadoes, hail, thunderstorms and forest fire. Flood extents include variants with and without protection. Regional climate-model and reanalysis products have different reference periods and scenarios, retained separately by member identity. Coverage: Individual native time-coverage fields and dates apply separately; no common interval is imposed. Geographic extent follows the named site or scope; unstated extents and sampling intervals remain unknown. Access: public 4TU.ResearchData metadata links describe the release. Formats: NetCDF, GeoTIFF and shapefile components, with PDF/RTF documentation and plain text. Licence: Varies by item and contributing collection. Cost and present file access are unverified. Caveats: Probability fields are model outputs, not verified forecasts or actual losses. A shared period, grid resolution or protection assumption is not asserted for all members. Simulation uses follow the source-defined purpose above. Related resources are retained in the same native collection with their distinct identities.

notes: Source metadata only. No distribution body, archive, model or executable file was acquired. Source statements are not independent performance verification. Grouped component identities and per-member terms are retained in member decisions. Individual native hazard members retain their own time coverage, climate baselines, scenario periods and licences. The forest-fire member describes daily probabilities of high forest-fire danger, not observed fire occurrence.
